claims.text: The initial CrFeCoNiSi alloy is a single-phase metallic solid solution with a homogeneous Si distribution.
An optimized pre-oxidation treatment enhances Si diffusion and uniform surface segregation in CrFeCoNiSi.
Surface-segregated Si oxidizes preferentially during pre-oxidation.
Preferential oxidation of Si produces an ultra-thin, continuous, adherent SiO2 interlayer at the metal/oxide interface.
The SiO2 interlayer has a low modulus and minimal thermal-expansion mismatch with the CrFeCoNiSi substrate.
The SiO2 interlayer suppresses deleterious residual stresses at the metal/oxide interface.
A continuous, adherent interlayer limits oxygen ingress and stabilizes the overall oxide scale.
Pre-treated CrFeCoNiSi will form a stable protective scale with minimal cracking or spallation at 950 °C.
Comparable CrFeCoNiMn or CrFeCoNiAl alloys will form poorly adhered, cracked, or spalled scales under the same oxidation conditions.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiAl lack the Si-diffusion and SiO2-interlayer mechanism proposed for CrFeCoNiSi.
The absence of Si diffusion in the Mn- or Al-containing baselines causes heterogeneous oxide nucleation and high residual stresses.
Heterogeneous nucleation and high residual stresses in the baseline alloys cause oxide cracking or spallation.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C in both oxidizing and corrosive atmospheres.
The mechanism may fail when Si diffusion is too slow to establish a uniform interlayer.
The comparison will use isothermal exposure at 950 °C in pure oxygen for up to 100 hours.
Failure to form a distinct, uniform SiO2 interlayer, or cracking and spallation comparable to the Mn- or Al-containing baselines, would falsify the hypothesis.
